name: Zebra Reveals Itself (Mimicry Hypothesis)
summary: PKD reports concluding in summer 1974 that the intelligence transmitting to him is a vast organism that camouflages itself by mimicking inanimate matter — he names it Zebra (after the African animal that hides in plain sight). All of nature, on this hypothesis, is alive and addressing him.
description: In summer 1974, PKD reports a sustained period of insight in which he concludes that the divine intelligence is not in heaven or in space but in the matter around him, mimicking inanimate objects — trash cans, rocks, vegetation. The intelligence camouflages itself as the way a zebra camouflages itself among savannah grasses. He gives it the name Zebra. The hypothesis stays with him through 1981 and is the central theological move of the late Exegesis: divinity is not transcendent; it is here, hiding by mimicry. The hypothesis is sourced to Bergson, Whitehead, and (after 1976) the Nag Hammadi gnostic texts.

pkd_interpretations.interpretation: VALIS is Zebra: a biological entity mimicking inanimate matter. The world is alive but in disguise.
Or perhaps Zebra is itself a manifestation of the orbital satellite VALIS.
Zebra is the central image in the novel.

scholar_interpretations.interpretation: McKee places Zebra within Whiteheadian process theology — God as continuously becoming through matter.
Davis frames Zebra as the most original PKD theological innovation.

primary_sources.excerpt: Hundreds of segments develop the Zebra hypothesis.
*VALIS* (1981) names Zebra as VALIS's modus operandi.

primary_quote: Zebra. Camouflaged nature God. Life form. VALIS.
